reviews.decision_reason: select_demand is the behaviorally significant fault. It filters for hard-coded fallback records n06-r07 and n06-r08, while the supplied corpus contains higher-scored records n06-r01 through n06-r06. Under the strict demand criteria, selecting lower-scored fallback rows without observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes visible in the package is not supported. The resulting output preserves only those two handoffs and drives the downstream recommendation toward n06-r07, but that recommendation is not grounded in the strongest supplied demand evidence.

normalize_evidence preserves the already-selected two rows and normalizes columns/types. Its output is incorrect only because select_demand supplied a demand set that is unsupported by the stricter criteria; no independent fault is visible in this boundary.

assemble_provenance ranks the normalized needs by demand_score and emits provenance rows matching the assigned output. The boundary is downstream of the faulty selection, so it propagates an unsupported demand set but does not introduce a separate localized defect.
